sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: **In the last lesson** we connected to Google ADK. **Today** we connect to the **OpenAI Agents SDK** — OpenAI's own agent framework.

sections.title: ① Real-World Analogy — The Hotel Concierge
sections.body: The OpenAI Agents SDK is like a hotel concierge. You (the user) tell the concierge what you need. The concierge knows all the hotel services (MCP tools) and coordinates them on your behalf. `MCPServerStdio` is the concierge's phonebook — the list of services (MCP servers) they can call.

sections.title: ② Plain English Explanation
sections.body:
The **OpenAI Agents SDK** (`openai-agents`) is OpenAI's official framework for building AI agents that use GPT models. It natively supports MCP through two classes:

- **`MCPServerStdio`** — connects to a local MCP server via stdio (subprocess)
- **`MCPServerHTTP`** — connects to a remote MCP server via HTTP

You create one of these, pass it to an `Agent`, and the agent automatically discovers and uses all the tools from your MCP server.

sections.title: ③ Installation
sections.body:
```bash
pip install openai-agents
# Make sure OPENAI_API_KEY is set in your environment
```

sections.title: ④ Complete Code Example
sections.body:
```python
# openai_agents_mcp.py
# OpenAI Agents SDK connected to your FastMCP server
# Install: pip install openai-agents
# Requires: OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable

import asyncio
import os
from agents import Agent, Runner             # OpenAI Agents SDK core
from agents.mcp import MCPServerStdio        # stdio MCP connector

# ─── STEP 1: Define the MCP server connection ─────────────────────────

async def run_openai_agent():
    """
    Create an OpenAI agent connected to our MCP calculator server.
    """
    print("🚀 Starting OpenAI Agent with MCP tools...")
    
    # MCPServerStdio defines HOW to connect to our server
    # It will launch the server as a subprocess when needed
    mcp_server = MCPServerStdio(
        params={
            "command": "python",                    # Launch command
            "args": ["fastmcp_full_server.py"],     # Server script
        },
        # cache_tools_list: if True, only fetches tool list ONCE (performance boost)
        # if False, fetches tools list on every agent run (always up to date)
        cache_tools_list=True    # Cache the tool list for better performance
    )
    
    # ── STEP 2: Create the Agent ───────────────────────────────────────
    
    # Agent is the OpenAI Agents SDK's main agent class
    agent = Agent(
        name="Math Assistant",               # Human-readable agent name
        model="gpt-4o",                      # OpenAI model to use
        instructions="""
        You are a precise and helpful math assistant.
        Always use the available calculator tools for computations — 
        never calculate in your head. Show each step of your work.
        After getting a tool result, explain what it means in plain English.
        """,
        mcp_servers=[mcp_server]             # List of MCP servers to connect to
    )
    
    # ── STEP 3: Run agent queries ──────────────────────────────────────
    
    questions = [
        "What is 999 times 888?",
        "Divide 50000 by 7 and round to 2 decimal places.",
        "I need to calculate: ((145 + 255) * 3) - 200. Work through it step by step."
    ]
    
    for question in questions:
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print(f"Question: {question}")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Runner.run() executes the agent with the given input
        # It handles the tool call loop automatically
        result = await Runner.run(
            starting_agent=agent,
            input=question          # The user's message
        )
        
        # The final output is in result.final_output
        print(f"Answer: {result.final_output}")

# ─── STEP 4: Demonstrate tool list caching ────────────────────────────

async def demonstrate_caching():
    """
    Show the difference between cached and non-cached tool lists.
    
    cache_tools_list=True:
      - Fetches tool list ONCE when agent first runs
      - Subsequent runs reuse the cached list
      - Faster, but won't see new tools added to the server
      
    cache_tools_list=False:
      - Fetches tool list on EVERY agent run
      - Always up-to-date with server changes
      - Slightly slower due to extra network round-trip
    """
    import time
    
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("TOOL LIST CACHING DEMONSTRATION")
    print("="*60)
    
    # Without caching
    server_no_cache = MCPServerStdio(
        params={"command": "python", "args": ["fastmcp_full_server.py"]},
        cache_tools_list=False   # Fetch fresh every time
    )
    
    # With caching
    server_with_cache = MCPServerStdio(
        params={"command": "python", "args": ["fastmcp_full_server.py"]},
        cache_tools_list=True    # Cache after first fetch
    )
    
    agent_cached = Agent(
        name="Cached Agent",
        model="gpt-4o",
        instructions="Answer math questions using tools.",
        mcp_servers=[server_with_cache]
    )
    
    print("\nWith cache_tools_list=True:")
    print("  First run  → fetches tools from server (~50ms)")
    print("  Second run → uses cached list (~0ms)")
    print("  Best for:  Servers whose tools don't change at runtime")
    
    print("\nWith cache_tools_list=False:")
    print("  Every run  → fetches tools from server (~50ms)")
    print("  Best for:  Servers that dynamically add/remove tools")

# ─── STEP 5: Compare MCPServerStdio vs MCPServerHTTP ─────────────────

def show_http_example():
    """
    Show how to connect to a REMOTE MCP server via HTTP.
    (This requires a server running at the URL — not starting one here)
    """
    from agents.mcp import MCPServerHTTP
    
    # MCPServerHTTP for remote servers
    # The server must already be running at this URL
    remote_server = MCPServerHTTP(
        url="http://your-server.example.com:8000/sse"
        # url: The SSE endpoint of your remote MCP server
        # This is the server started with: mcp.run(transport="sse", port=8000)
    )
    
    agent_with_remote = Agent(
        name="Remote Tool Agent",
        model="gpt-4o",
        instructions="You have access to remote tools.",
        mcp_servers=[remote_server]
    )
    
    print("\nMCPServerStdio vs MCPServerHTTP:")
    print("┌──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┐")
    print("│      MCPServerStdio          │       MCPServerHTTP            │")
    print("├──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┤")
    print("│ Launches server as subprocess│ Connects to already-running    │")
    print("│ Local machine only           │  server at a URL               │")
    print("│ stdio transport              │ Remote machines OK             │")
    print("│ Best for: development        │ HTTP+SSE transport             │")
    print("│ param: command + args        │ Best for: production           │")
    print("│                              │ param: url                     │")
    print("└──────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┘")

# ─── MAIN ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if not os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
        print("❌ Please set: export OPENAI_API_KEY='your-key-here'")
        exit(1)
    
    show_http_example()       # Show comparison table (no API needed)
    asyncio.run(run_openai_agent())   # Run the actual agent
```

sections.title: ⑥ Quick Recap — What Did We Just Learn?
sections.body:
- ✅ `MCPServerStdio` = connect to local MCP server (subprocess)
- ✅ `MCPServerHTTP` = connect to remote MCP server (URL)
- ✅ `cache_tools_list=True` = fetch tool list once (faster, use for stable servers)
- ✅ `Runner.run(agent, input)` = execute the agent with a user message
- ✅ OpenAI Agents SDK has MCP support built-in — no separate adapter needed

🎉 **All four frameworks connected! Next — keeping your MCP server secure!**
